chapter_metadata.title: Rapid Onsite Evaluation and Specimen Preparation
chapter_metadata.reference: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology, 2025

definitions.definition: Real‑time adequacy assessment and triage of cytology during bronchoscopy.
Conventional transbronchial needle aspiration without ultrasound guidance.
Centrifuged cytology pellet processed as FFPE for histology/IHC/FISH/NGS.
Remote ROSE using image streaming or robotic microscope control.

clinical_procedures.name: Two‑slide pull smear technique
steps: Expel aspirate onto slide A; use slide B to gently spread into two thin smears.
Air‑dry one slide for Diff‑Quik/Giemsa; fix the other in ethanol for Papanicolaou.
clinical_procedures.notes: Preferred by many cytopathologists for morphology.

clinical_procedures.name: ROSE adequacy workflow
steps: Assess for lymphoid tissue or lesional cells; note artifacts (mucus, ciliated cells, cartilage).
Communicate adequacy to bronchoscopist; adjust passes accordingly.
Allocate additional material to cell block (FFPE) for ancillary testing.

clinical_procedures.name: Cell block preparation (FFPE)
steps: Rinse residual material with ~50% ethanol and centrifuge to pellet.
Fix in formalin and embed in paraffin for IHC/FISH/NGS.
clinical_procedures.notes: Nontraditional preparations may be validated locally for molecular testing.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pass number optimization
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Balance adequacy vs tissue stewardship for molecular testing.
evidence: Chin 2002: increasing yield up to 7 passes; recommend 4 passes for malignancy.
Lee 2008: recommend 3 passes; at least one tissue core increases adequacy.
Yarmus 2013: four passes often adequate for molecular profiling (KRAS/EGFR/ALK).

recommendations: Plan pre‑analytic workflow to preserve tissue for ancillaries.
Prefer FFPE cell blocks for IHC/FISH; validate nontraditional prep when used.
ROSE may be used when available; ensure sufficient passes per station to achieve adequacy.
Obtain tissue for histology and broad biomarkers (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, NTRK1‑3, RET, METex14, ERBB2 (HER2), PD‑L1).
Consider up‑front slide sectioning for diagnostics/predictive testing with small samples.
Coordinate cytology staffing; recognize ROSE reimbursement constraints (CPT 88172 vs 88173/88331).
Telecytopathology can mitigate access/logistics where onsite coverage is limited.

Stop when diagnostic + molecular sufficiency reached

points: ROSE enhances efficiency of diagnostic bronchoscopy by reducing additional riskier procedures and enabling tissue stewardship for biomarker testing.
Diagnostic yield improvement is clear with cTBNA and mixed with EBUS‑TBNA; program benefits depend on local logistics and expertise.
Telecytopathology and standardized workflows broaden access while addressing reimbursement constraints.
